name: Cliff
tagline: Real-time streaming voice assistant for Android
description: Cliff is an Android voice assistant that delivers natural, low-latency conversation by streaming end to end: mic PCM streams into Deepgram Flux STT over a WebSocket, final transcripts are sent to Anthropic Claude via SSE, response text deltas are piped into Deepgram Aura-2 TTS as they arrive, and a barge-in controller cancels the LLM and squelches audio the instant the user interrupts.
generatedFrom: source code (authoritative); reflects the working tree, which differs from README.md in model/voice/language.

runtimeConfiguration.note: The pipeline is pinned to Japanese end-to-end. STT language_hint, the LLM system prompt, and the TTS voice must all agree because the Aura-2 voice is fixed for the life of its socket.
runtimeConfiguration.llmModel: claude-haiku-4-5 (active in ClaudeStreamingClient; claude-sonnet-4-6 is present but commented out)
runtimeConfiguration.readmeDivergence: README.md documents an English configuration (claude-sonnet-4-6, flux-general-en, aura-2-arcas-en). The code is the source of truth.

techStack.state: Kotlin Coroutines + StateFlow, MVVM (single ViewModel orchestrator)
techStack.llm: Anthropic Claude via Messages API with SSE streaming (https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages)
techStack.audio: AudioRecord (capture, 16 kHz PCM) + AudioTrack (playback, 48 kHz PCM)
techStack.networking: OkHttp 4.12.0 (shared client for HTTP + both WebSockets)

pipeline.summary: Mic -> Flux STT -> Claude -> Aura-2 TTS -> Speaker, with a barge-in controller straddling STT events, the LLM, and TTS.

stages.name: Mic Capture
stages.detail: AudioRecord captures 16 kHz mono PCM with hardware echo cancellation. Each ~20 ms frame is forwarded to Flux via flux.sendPcm(pcm) and also fed to updateMicLevel() to drive the visualizer.

stages.name: Deepgram Flux STT
stages.detail: WebSocket to Deepgram Flux (flux-general-multi, language_hint=ja, linear16, 16 kHz). Emits UserStart/UserStop turn events and Partial(text, isFinal) transcripts. Turn detection uses eot_threshold=0.85, eager_eot_threshold=0.85, eot_timeout_ms=8000. Audio captured before the socket opens is buffered (up to 50 frames) so the first syllable isn't lost.

stages.name: Turn dispatch & dedup
stages.detail: On a final Partial, the transcript is trimmed and compared to the last user message (exact match + areSimilar fuzzy check) to drop duplicates. New text is persisted (repo.addUserText) and passed to sendToLLM(). LatencyTracker.markRequestSent() stamps the TTFT clock here.

stages.name: Claude (Messages API, SSE)
stages.detail: Stateless HTTP POST per turn with stream=true, max_tokens=1024. The full conversation history plus the new user message is sent as the messages array, with the user-configurable system prompt as the top-level system field. Parses the SSE stream, emitting TextDelta on each content_block_delta text_delta and TextCompleted on message_stop. First TextDelta stamps LatencyTracker.markFirstToken() (TTFT).

stages.name: Deepgram Aura-2 TTS
stages.detail: Each Claude TextDelta is immediately streamed to Aura-2 (aura-2-uzume-ja, linear16, 48 kHz) via streamDelta() -> a serialized outbox Channel -> {"type":"Speak"}. On TextCompleted the ViewModel calls flush() ({"type":"Flush"}). Returned PCM is written to an AudioTrack (WRITE_BLOCKING); RMS of each buffer drives the visualizer at ~30 fps via onAudioLevel.

stages.name: Playback & routing
stages.detail: AudioTrack plays 48 kHz mono PCM under USAGE_VOICE_COMMUNICATION with transient-may-duck audio focus. Routing picks speaker vs. Bluetooth SCO / wired headset / earpiece (API 31+ setCommunicationDevice; legacy path below). An AudioDeviceCallback re-applies routing when devices are added/removed.

bargeIn.detail: Subscribes to Flux turn events. On UserStart it arms a 150 ms debounced job; if the user is still speaking after the delay, it calls llm.cancelResponse() (cancels the in-flight SSE request) and tts.stop() (squelch: drop incoming PCM, pause+flush AudioTrack, send Clear). UserStop disarms the pending job.

latency.exposedAs: VoiceAgentViewModel.latencyMs StateFlow, shown as an on-screen overlay

ServiceLocator.role: Manual dependency graph. init(ctx) builds a single shared OkHttpClient and wires repo, flux, llm, tts, audio, barge, prefsRepo.

VoiceAgentViewModel.role: Central orchestrator. Owns the startup gate, session lifecycle, STT->LLM->TTS wiring, audio routing, mic-level computation, and the visualizer/latency StateFlows.
VoiceAgentViewModel.state: AgentUiState (sessionId, sessionActive, livePartial, assistantLive, isThinking, error, messages, speakerOn)

BargeInController.role: 150 ms debounced interruption detection; cancels LLM and squelches TTS.

LlmClient.role: Streaming LLM interface. Defines Event (TextDelta/TextCompleted/Error) and DEFAULT_SYSTEM_MESSAGE (the Japanese Cliff persona).

ClaudeStreamingClient.role: LlmClient impl over the Anthropic Messages API with SSE parsing; stateless per request; cancellable in-flight.

FluxClient / FluxClientImpl.role: Deepgram Flux STT WebSocket; parses TurnInfo/Results messages into Partial + UserStart/UserStop events; buffers pre-open audio.

DeepgramTtsClient.role: Aura-2 TTS WebSocket + AudioTrack playback, audio focus, speakerphone routing, squelch/barge-in, and visualizer level callback.

PrefsRepository.role: Mints short-lived Deepgram and Claude credentials with the app key and caches each in memory until ~30 s before expiry.

PrefsApiClient.role: Minimal HTTP client for the two app-key-authenticated token endpoints under /api/{secret_path}.

LatencyTracker.role: TTFT measurement via markRequestSent / markFirstToken; exposes ttftMs.

AudioBlobVisualizer.role: Compose Canvas rendering 7 additively-blended orange orbs driven by max(ttsLevel, micLevel); orbit speed, breathing, and spread scale with amplitude.

dataModel.conversationStrategy: Stateless. Claude keeps no server-side session; the app resends the full history (system + all prior turns) on every request. Room persists it locally so context survives restarts.

security.principle: No long-lived API keys on device, and no server-side state. The app authenticates with two shared secrets and mints short-lived (10 min TTL) Deepgram and Claude credentials on demand.
security.authModel: Secret path segment in the API URL (CLIFF_SECRET_PATH) + app-key header X-Cliff-App-Key (CLIFF_APP_KEY). No device identity, no bearer token, no server-side state.
security.startupGate: On launch the app mints a Deepgram token as a connectivity preflight -> Ready on success (token cached for the first session). Failure -> Error screen with Retry.

backendContract.note: Cliff is client-only. It expects a backend serving these two endpoints under /api/{secret_path}; a stateless FastAPI reference lives in server/. Every request carries the X-Cliff-App-Key header.
backendContract.auth: X-Cliff-App-Key header + secret path segment; stateless (no bearer token, no device identity)

endpoints.notes: Server exchanges its Deepgram key via /v1/auth/grant so the raw key never leaves the backend.
